items.stem:
Read the following extract on the making of the Constituent Assembly and answer the questions that follow.
"The Muslim League chose to boycott the Constituent Assembly. The discussions in the Assembly were influenced by public opinion expressed through newspapers and submissions. The Constitution was framed between December 1946 and November 1949 in a time of great turmoil, including Partition."
(i) The members of the Constituent Assembly were elected by: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'Cabinet Mission' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The Congress dominated the Constituent Assembly. (2)
items.answer: (i) the provincial legislatures (ii) The British mission of 1946 whose plan provided for members of the Constituent Assembly to be elected by the provincial legislatures. (iii) The Muslim League boycotted it and the Congress had won most seats in the provincial elections of 1946.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) the provincial legislatures (ii) The British mission of 1946 whose plan provided for members of the Constituent Assembly to be elected by the provincial legislatures. (iii) The Muslim League boycotted it and the Congress had won most seats in the provincial elections of 1946.

items.stem:
Read the following statements about the Objectives Resolution and the will of the people:
I. Nehru wanted the Indian Constitution to copy the British model exactly.
II. Nehru referred to the American and French Revolutions while introducing the resolution.
III. Nehru said the Indian Constitution would not merely copy other models but would be adapted to Indian conditions.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: II and III only
items.markingKey: (a) I is incorrect: He wanted India to learn from others but adapt to Indian conditions. II is correct. III is correct.
options: II and III only
I only
II only
I and II only

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about defining rights in the Constituent Assembly:
I. Ambedkar opposed any safeguards for the depressed castes.
II. Separate electorates were opposed by most nationalists because they were seen as having divided the nation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: II only
items.markingKey: (b) I is incorrect: He argued for safeguards such as reservations. II is correct.
options: I only
II only
Both I and II
Neither I nor II

items.stem:
Read the following extract on defining rights in the Constituent Assembly and answer the questions that follow.
"The Constituent Assembly abolished untouchability and opened Hindu temples to all castes. Separate electorates were opposed by most nationalists because they were seen as having divided the nation. Ambedkar had demanded separate electorates for the depressed castes earlier, but in the Assembly he supported reservation."
(i) Which Muslim woman member of the Assembly opposed separate electorates? (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'reservation' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Jaipal Singh demanded protection for tribal peoples. (2)
items.answer: (i) Begum Aizaz Rasul (ii) The reservation of seats in legislatures and jobs in government for the depressed castes (Scheduled Castes). (iii) Adivasis had been dispossessed of their lands and marginalised and needed special safeguards.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) Begum Aizaz Rasul (ii) The reservation of seats in legislatures and jobs in government for the depressed castes (Scheduled Castes). (iii) Adivasis had been dispossessed of their lands and marginalised and needed special safeguards.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on the Objectives Resolution and the will of the people and answer the questions that follow.
"The Objectives Resolution provided for adequate safeguards for minorities, backward and tribal areas, and depressed and other backward classes. Nehru referred to the American and French Revolutions while introducing the resolution. Members argued that the Constitution must express the will of the people and not be imposed by the British."
(i) The Objectives Resolution proclaimed India to be an: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'will of the people' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Somnath Lahiri criticised the Constituent Assembly. (2)
items.answer: (i) 'Independent Sovereign Republic' (ii) The idea that the Constitution derived its authority from the people of India, not from the British. (iii) He felt it was working under the shadow of British imperialism and needed to be free of British influence.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) 'Independent Sovereign Republic' (ii) The idea that the Constitution derived its authority from the people of India, not from the British. (iii) He felt it was working under the shadow of British imperialism and needed to be free of British influence.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"Seats in legislatures and jobs in government were reserved for the lowest castes. Separate electorates were opposed by most nationalists because they were seen as having divided the nation. Ambedkar had demanded separate electorates for the depressed castes earlier, but in the Assembly he supported reservation. The Constituent Assembly abolished untouchability and opened Hindu temples to all castes."
(i) Explain the term 'depressed castes', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: Jaipal Singh demanded protection for tribal peoples. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "N.G. Ranga argued that the real minorities were the rich." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (2)
items.answer: (i) The castes subjected to untouchability, for whom B.R. Ambedkar demanded safeguards. (ii) Adivasis had been dispossessed of their lands and marginalised and needed special safeguards. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: He argued that the real minorities were the poor and downtrodden.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) The castes subjected to untouchability, for whom B.R. Ambedkar demanded safeguards. (ii) Adivasis had been dispossessed of their lands and marginalised and needed special safeguards. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: He argued that the real minorities were the poor and downtrodden.
